entry: Pre-Christian religion of the [[Slavs|Slavic peoples]], polytheistic and animistic and rooted in broader Proto-Indo-European religion. It centered on reverence for nature, ancestor worship and [[Ritual|rituals]] tied closely to the agricultural calendar. A unified pan-Slavic pantheon likely never existed because of geographic fragmentation, but certain core deities and cosmological concepts were shared across the East, West and South Slavs. Christianization between the 8th and 13th centuries was gradual and often superficial, especially in what is today Russia, and popular resistance led by volkhvs, pagan priests or shamans, recurred for centuries. The West Slavs of the Baltic withstood Christianity until the [[Northern Crusades]] imposed it by force. Many elements of the indigenous faith were incorporated into Slavic Christianity, and the worship of Slavic gods persisted in folk religion into modern times. Resistance to Christianity gave rise to a "whimsical [[Syncretism|syncretism]]" called dvoeverie, or "double faith."

Slovenian philosopher and cultural theorist. Žižek is a Global Distinguished Professor of German at [[New York University]] and a senior researcher at the University of Ljubljana. He is associated with the Ljubljana School of Psychoanalysis. He works mainly on continental philosophy, particularly Hegelianism, Lacanian [[Psychoanalysis|psychoanalysis]] and [[Marxism]], as well as political theory, film criticism and [[Theology|theology]]. He has written over 50 books, including *The Sublime Object of Ideology* (1989). His idiosyncratic style, with obscene jokes and [[Popular culture|pop culture]] examples, has brought him fame, controversy and criticism.

Peoples who speak the [[Slavic languages]], which belong to the Balto-Slavic branch of the Indo-European language family. Slavs live mainly in Central, Eastern and Southeastern Europe and Northern Asia, with large minorities in the Baltic states and Central Asia. Early Slavs came to control large parts of Central, Eastern and Southeast Europe between the sixth and seventh centuries, and they were gradually Christianized from the 7th century. By the 12th century they formed the core population of medieval states including [[Kievan Rus']], the Bulgarian Empire and [[Great Moravia]]. Present-day Slavs are classified as West Slavs, such as Poles and Czechs, East Slavs, such as Russians and Ukrainians, and South Slavs, such as Serbs and Bulgarians. Most Slavs are [[Christians]], but Bosniaks mostly identify as [[Muslims]].

American thrash metal band from Huntington Park, California, formed in 1981. Its fast, aggressive style made it one of the "big four" thrash bands, alongside [[Metallica]] and [[Megadeth]]. Its lyrics and album art cover [[Serial killer|serial killers]], [[Occult|occultism]], war and racism, drawing album bans and criticism from religious groups. Its third album, *Reign in Blood* (1986), is often described as one of the heaviest and most influential thrash metal albums. Slayer disbanded in 2019 after a farewell tour and has performed sporadic reunion shows since 2024.

Vehicle that slides across snow or ice on a smooth underside or runners. Some sleds are pulled by humans, animals or machines to carry passengers or cargo over level ground, while others travel downhill for recreation or competition. Evidence of sledges or skids used for transport dates to before 10,000 BC in North America and to by 3,200 BC in Sumer. Until the late 19th century, the closed winter sled, or vozok, provided fast transport across the snowy plains of European Russia and Siberia. British Arctic and Antarctic expeditions relied on man-hauled sledges, while dog sleds were used by most other expeditions, including those of [[Roald Amundsen]]. In American usage, sled often implies a smaller recreational device, while sledge implies a heavier sled for freight.

Sleep-related breathing disorder marked by repeated pauses in breathing during sleep. Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), caused by a blocked airway, is the most common form; central sleep apnea (CSA) occurs when the brain fails to signal breathing. Symptoms include daytime sleepiness, snoring and non-restorative sleep. OSA affects 936 million–1 billion people aged 30–69 worldwide. Untreated, it may increase the risk of [[Hypertension|hypertension]], [[Stroke|stroke]], [[Cardiovascular disease|cardiovascular disease]] and [[Diabetes|diabetes]]. Continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) machines improve outcomes with proper use, but more than half of users do not use them appropriately.

Medical disorder that disrupts a person's sleep patterns or sleep quality, with effects on physical, mental and emotional well-being. Sleep disorders are classified by the International Classification of Sleep Disorders into insomnia, sleep-related breathing disorders such as [[Sleep apnea|obstructive sleep apnea]], central disorders of hypersomnolence such as [[Narcolepsy]], circadian rhythm sleep disorders, parasomnias and sleep-related movement disorders. [[Insomnia]], difficulty falling or staying asleep without an obvious cause, is the most common. Contributing factors include increased medication use, age-related changes in [[Circadian rhythm|circadian rhythms]], stress, lifestyle changes and traumatic childhood experiences. Diagnosis commonly uses polysomnography and actigraphy, and sleep disturbances caused by mental, medical or substance abuse disorders should be managed by treating the underlying condition.

State of conscious paralysis that occurs while waking up or falling asleep. During an episode, which lasts no more than a few minutes, a person may [[Hallucination|hallucinate]] and often feels intense fear. It is believed to involve dysfunction in REM sleep and can be triggered by sleep deprivation or psychological stress. It occurs in healthy people as well as in those with [[Narcolepsy|narcolepsy]], and between 8% and 50% of people experience it at some point. Sleep paralysis has been linked to stories of alien abduction and other [[Paranormal|paranormal]] events.

Polyphyletic assemblage of mostly microscopic eukaryotic organisms, grouped in several distantly related clades. Slime molds have both single-celled and multicellular forms, and their cells come together to form [[Spore|spore]]-producing fruiting bodies. Most live in damp places such as rotting wood, where they help [[Decomposition|decompose]] dead vegetation, and some are parasitic. Plasmodial slime molds in the Myxogastria are visible to the naked eye. They are cosmopolitan, with some species in regions as dry as the [[Atacama Desert]] and as cold as the [[Arctic]]. Some species, such as *Physarum polycephalum*, have been used to simulate traffic networks. The first known account, by Thomas Panckow in 1654, described a "fast-growing fungus."

[[Weapon|Projectile weapon]] used to hand-throw a blunt missile such as a stone, clay or lead bullet. It has a central pouch between two cords; the thrower swings it in an arc and releases one cord at the precise moment, so the projectile flies ballistically toward its target. Slings have been used for [[Hunting|hunting]] and in combat, and they are inexpensive and easy to build. Slings are rare in the archaeological record because their materials are biodegradable, but slingstones have been reported from the Near East since the 6th millennium BC. The oldest surviving slings, radiocarbon dated to c. 2500 BC, were recovered from sites on the coast of Peru. Greeks and Romans used slings, and a pair of finely plaited slings was found in the tomb of [[Tutankhamun]].

Yugoslav and Serbian politician who was president of Serbia from 1989 to 1997 and of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia from 1997 until his overthrow in 2000. He played a major role in the [[Yugoslav Wars]] and was the first sitting head of state charged with war crimes. In May 1999, during the NATO bombing of Yugoslavia, the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia indicted him for crimes connected to the [[Kosovo War]]; later indictments concerned the Croatian War of Independence and the Bosnian War, including genocide charges. He denounced the tribunal as illegal and died of a heart attack in his cell in [[The Hague]] in 2006, before his trial concluded. After his death, the tribunal and its successor found that he was part of a joint criminal enterprise that used violence, including ethnic cleansing.

Gambling machine that creates a game of chance for its customers. A slot machine typically displays three or more reels that spin when play is activated, and it pays out according to the symbols that appear when they stop. Random number generators now control outcomes, though many machines retain a lever as a design feature. Slot machines are the most popular [[Gambling|gambling]] method in [[Casino|casinos]], contributing about 70% of the average U.S. casino's income. The term "one-armed bandit" alludes to early mechanical levers. An 1893 design by Sittman and Pitt of [[Brooklyn]] was based on poker, and between 1887 and 1895 Charles Fey of San Francisco devised a simpler three-reel machine with a Liberty Bell symbol that made automatic payouts practical.

Bear species native to the [[Indian subcontinent]], also called the Indian bear. It is the only species in the genus *Melursus* and feeds on [[Termite|termites]], [[Ant|ants]] and fruit, sucking up insects with its long lower lip. It has long, shaggy fur, a mane around the face and sickle-shaped claws. It is listed as vulnerable on the IUCN Red List, mainly because of habitat loss and degradation. Humans have reduced its habitat and killed it for food and for products such as its claws and bacula. Sloth bears have also been tamed as performing animals and pets.

Neotropical xenarthran mammal of the suborder Folivora, noted for its slow movement. Tree sloths spend most of their lives hanging upside down in the [[Tropical rainforest|rainforests]] of South and Central America. Seven extant species belong to two genera, the three-toed *Bradypus* and the two-toed *Choloepus*, although all sloths have three toes on each rear limb. Sloths are most closely related to [[Anteater|anteaters]], and together they make up the order Pilosa. Their slowness allows a low-energy diet of leaves and helps them avoid predators that hunt by sight, while green algae living in their fur provide camouflage. Ground sloths, some up to the size of elephants, died out in the Quaternary extinction around 12,000 years ago.

Landlocked country in Central Europe, officially the Slovak Republic, with a population exceeding 5.4 million. Its capital and largest city is [[Bratislava]]. Its territory was part of the Kingdom of Hungary before it became part of Czechoslovakia, which was proclaimed in 1918. After a Soviet-backed coup in 1948, Czechoslovakia became a communist state, and the Velvet Revolution ended communist rule in 1989. Slovakia became independent on 1 January 1993 after the peaceful dissolution of Czechoslovakia. It is a member of the [[European Union]], [[NATO]], the [[Schengen Area]] and the [[OECD]], and it is home to eight UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Known as the "European Detroit," it is the world's largest per-capita car producer, making 1.08 million cars in 2023, with the automotive sector accounting for 44% of industrial output.

Country in Central Europe, bordered by Italy, Austria, Hungary and Croatia. Its capital and largest city is [[Ljubljana]]. Mostly mountainous and forested, it covers 20,271 sq km (7,827 sq mi) and has a population of about 2.1 million. Its official language is Slovene. [[Slavs|Slavic tribes]], the ancestors of modern Slovenes, arrived in the 5th century AD, and the territory later belonged to many states, including the Kingdom of Hungary and the Habsburg Empire. Slovenia became one of six constituent republics of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia in 1945 and declared independence in June 1991, after the brief Ten-Day War. Its high-income economy spans manufacturing, information technology, financial services and tourism, and the country is a member of the [[European Union]] and [[NATO]].

Nocturnal primate of the genus *Nycticebus*, native to [[Southeast Asia]]. Slow lorises range from [[Bangladesh]] and northeast India to the [[Philippines]], and from China's Yunnan province to [[Java]]. At least eight species are recognized, and a ninth, the pygmy slow loris, was moved to the genus *Xanthonycticebus*. They have large eyes, a round head and a toxic bite, produced by licking a sweat gland on the arm and mixing the secretion with saliva; the toxin is used mainly in disputes within the species. They move slowly and deliberately, and when threatened they stop and remain motionless. All slow lorises are threatened by the wildlife trade and habitat loss, and demand from the exotic pet trade and [[Traditional medicine|traditional medicine]] has been the greatest cause of decline.

Densely populated urban residential area of weak housing, often associated with [[Poverty|poverty]]. Slum residences range from shanties to deteriorated but professionally built dwellings, and most lack reliable sanitation, clean water, electricity and law enforcement. The [[United Nations]] defines slums as informal settlements lacking one or more of the following: access to improved water, access to improved sanitation, sufficient living area, housing durability and security of tenure. Slums became common in the United States and Europe in the 19th to late 20th centuries and are still predominantly found in developing countries, where the world's largest slum city is Orangi in [[Karachi]], Pakistan. Causes include rapid rural-to-urban migration, high unemployment, poor planning and natural disasters. Strategies include slum removal, relocation, upgrading and public housing.

Dwarf irregular galaxy near the [[Milky Way]], currently one of its satellites, about 200,000 light-years away. It is visible from the entire Southern Hemisphere and lies across the constellation Tucana and part of Hydrus. The galaxy contains several hundred million stars and has a total mass of approximately 7 billion solar masses. It forms a pair with the [[Large Magellanic Cloud]] and is likely a former satellite of that companion. In 1908 Henrietta Swan Leavitt published a study of its variable stars, revealing a period–luminosity relation for [[Cepheid variable|Cepheid variables]] that became a basis for measuring distances. In 1913 Ejnar Hertzsprung first estimated the distance to the galaxy using that relation.

Corporation, partnership or sole proprietorship with few employees or low annual revenue. Qualifications vary by country and industry: the U.S. Small Business Administration uses fewer than 500 employees for many programs, while the [[European Union]] uses 50. Small businesses often include [[Retail|retail]] and service operations, and professionals such as [[Lawyer|lawyers]] and [[Medical doctor|doctors]] may operate as small businesses. Owner-managers often do not distinguish personal and business interests, and lenders may seek personal guarantees.

Organ of the gastrointestinal tract where most nutrients are absorbed. It lies between the [[Stomach|stomach]] and the [[Large intestine]], receives bile and pancreatic juice, and is about 6.5 meters (21 feet) long, though it is narrower in diameter than the large intestine. It has three regions: the duodenum, where preparation for absorption begins; the jejunum, specialized for absorbing nutrients previously digested by enzymes; and the ileum, which mainly absorbs [[Vitamin B12|vitamin B12]], bile salts and remaining products of digestion. Folds, villi and microvilli enlarge its surface area, which averages 30 square meters (320 sq ft).

Vaccine used to prevent [[Smallpox|smallpox]], a contagious disease caused by the variola virus. In 1796 British physician [[Edward Jenner]] showed that infection with the milder cowpox virus conferred immunity, and it is the first vaccine developed against a contagious disease. From 1958 to 1977 the [[World Health Organization]] led a global vaccination campaign that eradicated smallpox, the only human disease to be eradicated. The term vaccine derives from *vacca*, the Latin word for cow. Routine vaccination of the general public has ended, but the vaccine is still produced for research and to guard against bioterrorism. First-generation vaccines, which contain live vaccinia virus, can cause serious side effects, including death in 1–10 people per million vaccinations. Three smallpox vaccines have been approved in at least one country for preventing mpox.

Handheld mobile device that combines a mobile phone with advanced computing. Smartphones have a [[Touchscreen|touchscreen]] interface, built-in [[Camera|cameras]], GPS navigation and mobile operating systems that run downloadable applications. They contain metal–oxide–semiconductor integrated circuit chips and sensors such as accelerometers, barometers and gyroscopes, and they support wireless standards including LTE, 5G NR, [[Wi-Fi]], [[Bluetooth]] and satellite navigation. Following the rising popularity of the [[IPhone|iPhone]] in the late 2000s, most smartphones adopted thin, slate-like forms with large multi-touch screens rather than physical keyboards. Smartphones have largely replaced personal digital assistants, portable media players and point-and-shoot cameras. In 2019, 1.54 billion smartphone units were shipped worldwide, and their use has been associated with both convenience and negative physical, mental and cognitive effects.

Family of small fishes, the Osmeridae, found in the North Atlantic and North Pacific oceans and in rivers, streams and lakes of Europe, North America and Northeast Asia. Most species rarely exceed 20 centimeters (8 in), although some female European smelt reach 25–40 cm. Many are anadromous, living most of their lives at sea but traveling into fresh water to breed. Some species run in large schools along coastlines during spring migration, and they are often fried and eaten whole. In Canadian provinces and U.S. states around the [[Great Lakes]], smelt dipping is a common group sport in early spring. The Delta smelt of California and the eulachon are protected from harvest, and the earliest known fossil smelt is *Enoplophthalmus* from the Early Oligocene of Europe.

Process of applying heat and a chemical reducing agent to [[Ore|ore]] to extract a desired base metal. It is a form of [[Metallurgy|extractive metallurgy]] used to obtain metals such as iron, copper, silver, tin and lead. The reducing agent is commonly carbon, such as carbon monoxide from incomplete combustion of [[Coke (fuel)|coke]] or, in earlier times, of [[Charcoal]]. Sulfide ores such as those of copper, zinc and lead are roasted first to convert the sulfides to oxides, which are more readily reduced to metal. Iron ore is smelted in a blast furnace to produce [[Pig iron]], which is converted into [[Steel]]. Because [[Aluminium|aluminum]] forms a very stable compound with oxygen, it is instead smelted by electrolytic reduction of aluminum oxide dissolved in molten cryolite.
